newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Taiwan statement circulated, with U.N. disclaimer.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan statement circulated, with U.N. disclaimer.

text.p: A statement by Taiwan's foreign ministry was circulated as a U.N. document on Monday at the request of the Solomon Islands but accompanied by a disclaimer by the U.N. secretariat.
The Solomon Islands is one of a number of countries that support U.N. membership for Taiwan, regarded by China as a renegade province.
Taiwan's statement, originally issued by its foreign ministry last July, was largely a restatement of arguments supporting its bid for a U.N. seat.
But because of China's strong opposition to any move -- at the United Nations or anywhere else -- suggesting Taiwan is an independent entity, the U.N. secretariat added the unusual disclaimer.

Noting the Solomon Islands letter and accompanying Taiwan statement had been "reproduced as received," it added: "The designations employed do not imply the expression of any opinion whatsoever on the part of the Secretariat of the United Nations concerning the legal status of any country, territory or area, or of its authorities."

The Solomon Islands U.N. envoy Rex Horoi said he was requesting circulation of Taiwan's statement in response to a complaint by China's U.N. ambassador Qin Huasun last October protesting against the latest move to seat Taiwan.

Each year since 1993, a group of fewer than 20 mostly African, Central American and Caribbean countries has called for the inscription of a new item on the General Assembly's agenda aimed at establishing a committee to consider U.N. membership for Taiwan.
The move has been blocked each time in the Assembly's steering committee.
